reason: The text narrative supports this statement through multiple indicators: (1) David explicitly expresses faith that Yahweh will protect and deliver Israel from the Philistine threat ('The Lord [Yahweh] who delivered me from the paw of the lion and the paw of the bear will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine'); (2) David invokes Yahweh's name and declares 'the battle is the Lord's' before fighting Goliath; (3) The narrative shows Yahweh providing victory and deliverance to Israel through David's defeat of Goliath, resulting in the Philistine army's retreat. The text demonstrates Yahweh acting protectively on Israel's behalf against an existential threat, which is consistent with Yahweh desiring their wellbeing.
